headline: Oil soars past US$100 after new US attacks on Iranian ships
summary: The Brent barrel crossed the $100 mark again and reached its highest price since July after new US attacks on Iranian ships.
why: Brent is the main international benchmark for crude oil, so Gulf military escalation that threatens shipping quickly feeds into global fuel costs, inflation expectations and energy-company margins.
why_moved: New US attacks on Iranian ships raised fears of supply disruption in the Gulf, lifting Brent above $100 to its highest level since July.
